lastCompletedStory.title: Wire the recycle watcher into cam run and prove SIGTERM+respawn end-to-end

nextStoryContext: cam run now spawns cam orch-recycle-watch (via spawnWatcherFn / spawnWatcherDefault) alongside the sidecar in the if (result.created) block. The watcher is killed in the SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup handler alongside the sidecar. makeResolvePidFn in orch-recycle-watch.ts was fixed to take the LAST pgrep line (highest PID = child claude, not the bash wrapper parent which starts first and has a lower PID). SpawnWatcherFn type is exported from run.ts; tests inject noopWatcher to prevent real watcher spawn. The integration test (test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts) uses a bash fake-claude that writes a handoff file on SIGTERM; it proves end-to-end: arming ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER -> watcher fires SIGTERM -> bash wrapper respawns (ORCH_SESSION_MARKER changes to new UUID). Follow-up CAM-164 tracks the real-claude SIGTERM ceremony (operator-validated). US-005 is the next story: explicit rehydrate delivery on respawn via CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE env var in buildOrchestratorPaneCommand.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed: proc.pid is readonly number, proc.kill() exists, cwd and stdio (file descriptor number) options are valid. spawnWatcherDefault implementation matches documented API.
